newsitem.title: USA: Ill. unemployment down 0.2 pct in April.
newsitem.headline: Ill. unemployment down 0.2 pct in April.

text.p: Illinois unemployment dipped 0.2 percent in April to a seasonally adjusted 4.8 percent, marking the lowest level since 1974, the Illinois Department of Employment Security announced Tuesday.

The number of unemployed workers in April hit the lowest ebb since August of 1979, marked by significant job growth in transportation, services, manufacturing and finance-insurance-real estate sectors over April 1996, the department reported.
Initial claims for unemployment insurance in the first four months of the year were down 12 percent over the same period in 1996, the department reported.

The seasonally adjusted unemployment for April 1996 was 5.3 percent and the results from the last month marked the sixth consecutive month in which the Illinois rate fell below the national rate, the department reported.

Total jobs rose 79,230 over the April 1996 numbers, with the transportation-communications-public utilities sector logging a 3.3 percent increase of 10,800 jobs, the department reported. Services sector generated a 46,200 gain with a 2.8 percent increase, the department reported.
Manufacturing recorded a 1.2 percent increase and finance-insurance-real estate marked a 1.1 percent increase, the department reported.
